methodological_rigor.justification: This is an in vitro, multi-cell-line study testing dexamethasone (DEX) sensitivity across five ALL cell lines (Jurkat, MOLT-3, REH, RS4;11, CCRF–CEM) with time-course viability counts and flow-cytometry phenotyping (MDC/Annexin V/PI) to relate autophagy and cell death (Results 3.1–3.3). The design is coherent for a mechanistic screen and includes a receptor-perturbation check using the GR antagonist Ru486 to probe GR dependence (Results 3.2). However, inference is limited by reliance on pharmacologic modulators and a fluorescent autophagy dye readout without orthogonal genetic or flux validation, and there is no in vivo or primary-sample confirmation. Statistics are described as Prism-based ANOVA with appropriate post hoc tests across ≥ 3 biological replicates, but reporting is largely p-value oriented without effect sizes/CI or a prespecified analysis plan (Methods 2.6).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The work addresses a clinically important problem (glucocorticoid resistance in ALL) and tests druggable modulation of autophagy, including use of clinically available agents such as tamoxifen, as co-treatments with DEX (Abstract; Results 3.4–3.5). The outcomes are cell viability/proliferation and apoptosis/necrosis readouts rather than patient endpoints, and all experiments are in established cell lines. As presented, the translational path is plausible but not demonstrated in vivo or in patient-derived material. On Oxford CEBM, the evidence level is basic science preclinical work (LoE 5).

reporting_quality.justification: No single standard (CONSORT/STROBE/PRISMA/etc.) fits a cell-line pharmacologic modulation paper, so 'other' is appropriate. The Methods are generally specific about cell culture conditions, reagents/doses, and assay workflows (e.g., trypan blue counts; MDC/Annexin V/PI staining; flow cytometer acquisition and gating basics; Methods 2.3–2.4). The normalized manuscript does not include a clear data/code availability statement or public deposition of raw flow cytometry files/analysis scripts, limiting reproducibility beyond the procedural description. Many results are figure-referenced rather than fully tabulated in text.

novelty_literature.justification: The manuscript offers a meaningful extension of existing literature by comparing multiple DEX-sensitive and -resistant ALL cell lines side-by-side and testing both induction and inhibition of autophagy as sensitization strategies (Results 3.1, 3.4). The central idea that autophagy modulation can influence glucocorticoid response is established, and the novelty is mainly in the specific cross-line patterns and the emphasis on an ‘optimal basal autophagy’ framing with tamoxifen as a broadly effective sensitizer (Results 3.5; Discussion).

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with clear sectioning and a logical flow from baseline DEX sensitivity through GR perturbation to autophagy modulation experiments (Results 3.1–3.5). Methods are described with concrete experimental parameters, and the Discussion is appropriately caveated about heterogeneity and mechanistic complexity. Minor tightening would come from more explicit quantitative summaries in text rather than relying on figure calls.

key_strengths: Uses a panel of five ALL cell lines spanning DEX-sensitive and -resistant phenotypes and triangulates viability with apoptosis/necrosis and an autophagy-associated dye readout over time (Results 3.1, 3.3).

Includes mechanistic perturbation of glucocorticoid receptor signaling (Ru486) and systematic testing of multiple pharmacologic autophagy modulators, highlighting tamoxifen as a broadly acting sensitizer (Results 3.2, 3.4–3.5).
key_concerns: Evidence is limited to established cell lines with pharmacologic probes; key mechanistic claims about autophagy would be stronger with orthogonal flux assays and/or genetic perturbations and with validation in primary or in vivo models.

Statistical reporting is adequate at a basic level (replicates and ANOVA/post hoc), but lacks effect sizes/CI and more transparent handling of multiplicity across many conditions and time points (Methods 2.6; Results 3.4).
No explicit data/code availability statement or public release of raw assay outputs is present in the normalized manuscript, constraining reproducibility.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a competent preclinical pharmacology/mechanism study with a clear clinical motivation and reasonably executed cell-line experiments, but it remains hypothesis-generating without in vivo or patient-derived confirmation. The highest plausible venue tier is a solid specialty/basic-translational journal contingent on strengthening autophagy-specific evidence, sharpening claims, and improving reproducibility disclosures.
